method: Ghidra DecompInterface (pyghidra open_project API) + raw byte disassembly of wpcmk.ovr. Functions decompiled: wpcmk_pick_portrait_loop (0x4bad), portrait_load_from_disk (0x4a9a), ui_draw_portrait_frame (0x0c12), wpcmk_change_portrait (0x5422). Key bytes verified against the original/wpcmk.ovr binary. Cross-referenced against wpcmk-screen-flow.json (screen-10), wpcmk-window-layouts.json (screen-10-portrait), wpcmk-msg-strings.json (msgs 0x458/0x459), and portrait-pools.json. DELTA=0 for wpcmk (file offset = CS offset).

findings.claim: wpcmk_pick_portrait_loop (0x4bad) cycles ALL 42 portraits (indices 0..41) with NO race/sex/class filter. The loop body contains zero comparisons against *0x560d (race), *0x560e (alignment), or *0x560f (class). All 42 portraits are always available to any character regardless of race, sex, or class.

evidence.decompile_excerpt: do { if (*(byte *)0x560c != uVar2) { portrait_load_from_disk(); uVar2 = (uint)*(byte *)0x560c; } ui_draw_portrait_frame(); iVar1 = input_poll_key_or_mouse(); ... if (iVar1 == 1) { *(undefined1 *)0x560c = (char)((*(byte *)0x560c + 0x29) % 0x2a); } else if (iVar1 == 3) { *(undefined1 *)0x560c = (char)((*(byte *)0x560c + 1) % 0x2a); } } while (iVar1 != 5);
evidence.note: The loop body reads only from *0x560c (portrait index cache). No conditional branches on *0x560d, *0x560e, *0x560f, or any other character-state variables exist within the loop.

findings.claim: portrait-pools.json finding 'portrait-dispatch-by-class' misidentifies address 0x3c49 as a portrait dispatcher. 0x3c49 is actually the STARTER ITEM dispatcher (confirmed by wpcmk-screen-flow.json screen-11 and wpcmk-naming-pass.json). The 5 per-class values ([141,130,132,135,8] for Fighter etc.) are ITEM IDs not portrait reference values. Cross-verification: Fighter item IDs match exactly: screen-flow Fighter items = [0x08,0x87,0x84,0x82,0x8d] = [8,135,132,130,141] (same set, different order). Furthermore, portrait-pools.json field 'portraitIndex at pcfile +0x1ab' (DGROUP 0x561b) is a DISTINCT byte from the portrait picker's output field at record +0x19c (DGROUP 0x560c). The SPD+1 formula writes to 0x561b (a separate field), not to the portrait picker's record field at 0x560c.

evidence.note: Two separate character-record bytes. 0x560c = player-selected portrait (0..41). 0x561b = SPD+1 derived value (separate, purpose unclear but confirmed by SPD+1 asm at 0x4ded: a0 a1 55 fe c0 a2 1b 56).

findings.claim: Portrait picker key bindings: key 1 = previous portrait (index decrements with wrap), key 3 = next portrait (index increments with wrap), key 5 = accept/confirm (exits loop). Both navigation keys wrap fully around all 42 portraits. Mouse button mapping (when *0x4fc4==1): button 0 -> key 1 (prev), button 1 -> key 3 (next), button 2 -> key 5 (accept).

0x4d3c: cmp ax, 0; je 0x4d27  ; button 0 -> map to key 1
0x4d41: cmp ax, 1; je 0x4d2e  ; button 1 -> map to key 3
0x4d46: cmp ax, 2; je 0x4d35  ; button 2 -> map to key 5

evidence.key_comparisons_at: 0x4d7a: cmp ax, 1 (key1 branch); 0x4d7f: cmp ax, 3 (key3 branch); 0x4d82: cmp [bp-2], 5 (exit test)

findings.claim: Portrait navigation wraps fully in both directions: key 1 (prev) uses (idx+41)%42 which wraps index 0 to 41; key 3 (next) uses (idx+1)%42 which wraps index 41 to 0. Both formulas use signed IDIV by 42 to compute the modulo.

Starting portrait index on screen-10 entry is ALWAYS 0 for new character creation. Before calling wpcmk_pick_portrait_loop, wpcmk_create_character_master writes c6 06 0c 56 00 (mov byte [0x560c], 0) at 0x4ed0, clearing the cache. The loop initializes its 'previous' cache (uVar2) to 0xffff, so the first iteration always calls portrait_load_from_disk to load portrait 0. For CHANGE PORTRAIT (wpcmk_change_portrait, 0x5422): the starting index is the CHARACTER'S CURRENT portrait (loaded from record into *0x560c by the preceding roster_io call). For new creation, portrait 0 is always first shown.

evidence.master_clear_parse: mov byte [0x560c], 0  ; clear portrait_idx cache to 0
evidence.master_call_parse: call 0x4bad  ; call portrait picker loop (target verified: 0x4ed8+0xfcd5-0x10000=0x4bad)
evidence.change_portrait_load: 0x542b: call 0x51c6 (load char record); 0x542f: mov al,[0x560c] -> portrait idx from loaded record
evidence.sentinel: uVar2 = 0xffff (c7 46 fc ff ff at 0x4c37) ensures first-iteration load always fires regardless of index value

findings.claim: portrait_load_from_disk (0x4a9a) loads one portrait descriptor from the appropriate video-mode file. File selection: EGA bit (0x4fc6 & 1) -> WPORT1.EGA (template at 0x53d2); VGA bit (0x4fc6 & 2) -> WPORT1.CGA (0x53dd); CGA bit (0x4fc6 & 4) -> WPORT1.CGA variant (0x53e8); Herc bit (0x4fc6 & 8) -> WPORT1.T16 (0x53f3). File-number digit = (param_1 / 14) + '1' (giving suffix '1','2','3'). Seek offset = (param_1 % 14) * stride * 9, where stride=0x20 (EGA/Herc) or 0x10 (VGA/CGA). Descriptor sizes: 0x120 (288) bytes per portrait in EGA; 0x90 (144) bytes in CGA. After load, calls func 0xdcf2 (wroot image 0x2256) to blit/decompress the portrait data to screen.

evidence.decompile_excerpt: if ((*(uint *)0x4fc6 & 1) == 0) { ... CGA/Herc branches ... } else { func_0x0000f3aa(local_18, 0x53d2); } local_13 = (char)(param_1 / 0xe) + '1'; func_0x0000f0dc(); func_0x0000c772(local_18, 0); local_4 = func_0x0000f924(); if (local_4 == -1) { func_0x0000bb71(); } func_0x0000fdbd(local_4); func_0x0000fd6f(); func_0x0000fda5(); func_0x0000dcf2();
evidence.file_digit_parse: mov ax,[bp+4]; mov cx,14; cwd; idiv cx -> ax=idx/14, dx=idx%14; add ax,'1' -> digit char; mov [buf-dig], al
evidence.seek_formula_parse: mov ax,param1(=idx%14); imul [bp-0x18](=stride); mov dx,ax; shl ax,3; add ax,dx; cwd -> push dx:ax = (idx%14)*stride*9

findings.claim: The portrait index written to the character record is the final value of *0x560c when key 5 is pressed. This is at record offset 0x19c (= 0x560c - 0x5470). The loop does NOT write to the record itself; the entire 432-byte record buffer at *0x5470 is committed to disk at screen-16 (save step) by roster_io_one_record. The byte at *0x560c (record +0x19c) is therefore the player-selected portrait index.

evidence.write_via: roster_io_one_record (0x001b mode=1) writes 432 bytes from *0x5470 to PCFILE.DBS at screen-16

findings.claim: The portrait picker uses two messages in *0x56ca (the navigation instructions window): msg 0x458 = '\x11\x12 TO REVIEW PORTRAITS' at cursor row 9, col 1; msg 0x459 = 'PRESS \x15 TO SELECT' at cursor row 0x0c, col 2. (\x11 and \x12 are keyboard-arrow glyphs; \x15 is the '5' key or ENTER glyph in the game's font.) A third message is written via ui_write_centered_msg (0x638) with msg 0x45f in the *0x56cc portrait frame window.

evidence.cursor_setup_458: 0x4bfd: push 0x12 (row?); push [0x56ca]; call bda7 before msg 0x458
evidence.cursor_setup_459: 0x4c1d: push 2; push 0xc; push [0x56ca]; call bda7 before msg 0x459

findings.claim: Portrait picker uses two windows: *0x56cc (image area, x=21 y=7 w=19 h=13) for the portrait frame display, and *0x56ca (prompt, x=0 y=20 w=40 h=5) for navigation instructions. Both are pre-existing persistent windows (not created by this function). Both are cleared at entry via ui_window_clear (thunk 0xed5a) and refreshed via func_e5b5. No new windows are created.

Total portrait count = 42 (0x2a). Portraits 0..13 in WPORTx.EGA/CGA/T16 file 1, 14..27 in file 2, 28..41 in file 3. The modulo divisor 0x2a = 42 is hardcoded in both key-1 and key-3 navigation arithmetic.

filter_formula: NONE: all 42 portraits are available to all characters regardless of race (0x560d), alignment (0x560e), or class (0x560f). The loop has no conditional branches on character-state fields.

default_index: For new character creation: always 0. wpcmk_create_character_master clears *0x560c to 0 at 0x4ed0 (bytes: c6 06 0c 56 00) immediately before calling portrait loop. The loop's cache sentinel uVar2=0xffff ensures portrait 0 is always loaded on first display. For CHANGE PORTRAIT (0x5422): starting index is the character's current portrait loaded from the roster record.
open_questions: The centered message at 0x45f (call to ui_write_centered_msg with msg 0x45f at 0x4c3f) was not decoded in the msg-strings pass. Its text is unknown.

The 4x func_c6b2 calls (wroot 0x0c16) in the init section register mouse-click hotspot regions. Their exact coordinate args read from the *0x56ca window struct bytes [+2] and [+3]. The meaning of those struct fields (likely width and height) and the resulting hotspot geometry is not fully documented here.

portrait_load_from_disk ends with a call to func 0xdcf2 (wroot image 0x2256). This function processes/blits the loaded portrait data. Its exact behavior (decompression, palette mapping, blit-to-window) is not traced here.

WPORT files: whether file 0x53dd uses exactly WPORT1.CGA or a different CGA variant. The decompile shows 4 template branches but only 3 file-pattern names were found at 0x608d/0x6098/0x60ae. The exact string at 0x53dd/0x53e8/0x53f3 was not read in this pass.

The separate byte at record +0x1ab (*0x561b) written by SPD+1 formula (portrait-pools.json finding) -- its actual runtime purpose is unclear. It may be an 'initial portrait suggestion' used elsewhere, or dead code, or related to wpcvw portrait display.
